name: Prepaid Variable Forward (PVF) / Collar-Plus-Loan
summary: A collar on a concentrated share position combined with a loan against the collared stock, converting an unsellable holding into cash today while the option band defines how many shares are ultimately delivered.

legs.strike_rule: the existing concentrated position, 100 shares per unit, held as loan collateral
|put delta| 0.30-0.40, at the floor price the lender will advance against
call delta 0.20-0.30, at the upper participation limit; strike solved so the collar is zero-cost

max_profit: (call strike - basis) x 100 plus whatever the advanced cash earns; upside above the call strike is surrendered
max_loss: (basis - put strike) x 100 plus net collar cost; below the floor the lender keeps the shares and the loan is extinguished
breakevens: basis +/- the net collar cost per share

greeks.delta: +30 to +50 per unit inside the band, collapsing toward zero at both strikes
greeks.gamma: negative near the call strike, positive near the put

when_to_use: A single holding is too large a share of the account to keep unhedged but cannot or should not be sold (tax lot, restriction, conviction). The collar caps and floors it; the loan turns the floored value into deployable cash. Note this is a financing structure, not an alpha structure.
entry_rules: OPTIONS LEGS ARE LEVEL 3 AND PERMITTED. THE FINANCING LEG IS NOT AVAILABLE HERE: Alpaca does not offer non-purpose lending against a collared position, so on this account the structure degrades to a long-dated zero-cost collar plus ordinary margin borrowing, which is not the same thing and must be logged as such.
Position must be >= 20% of account equity to justify the structure; below that use a plain collar.
Put strike >= 85% of spot (the advance rate a real PVF would lend against); call strike set so net collar cost <= 0.5% of share notional.
Both legs same expiry, 270+ DTE, OI >= 250, single MLeg order against the existing shares.
If ordinary margin is used as the financing substitute, borrow <= 50% of the put strike's notional and log the interest rate; never borrow above the floor.
No ex-dividend date within 5 trading days of expiration.
management_rules: Roll the entire collar out at 90 DTE, keeping the floor at or above the outstanding borrow.
If spot rises more than 15% above the call strike, do not chase it by rolling the call up unless the roll is a credit - the surrendered upside was the price of the cash.
Repay borrowings from any dividends received on the collared shares.
Re-test quarterly: if the position has fallen below 10% of equity, unwind the structure - it no longer earns its complexity.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: the short call is the assignable leg; close it by 15:30 ET on expiration day whenever it is ITM, and before every ex-dividend date while ITM - assignment would sell the collateral out from under the borrowing.
Close the short call at extrinsic < $0.10 or delta >= 0.85.
Close the long put rather than exercising it; exercising would sell the shares at the floor and must be a deliberate decision, not an expiry default.
Unwind in strict order: repay borrowings, then close the short call, then the long put, then decide on the shares.
assignment_risk: One assignable short call against collateralized shares. In a real PVF the delivery is contractual at maturity; in this replication an early assignment liquidates the collateral while the loan is still outstanding, which is the single failure mode that matters.
buying_power: Shares are already held; the short call is share-covered. Any financing leg consumes margin and interest at the broker's rate.
liquidity_needs: Long-dated chain with real OI - realistically ETFs and mega-caps only; a genuinely concentrated small-cap position cannot be collared at 730 DTE.
common_mistakes: Borrowing above the floor, which reintroduces exactly the downside the collar removed; treating margin borrowing as equivalent to a non-purpose PVF loan (the margin call behavior is completely different); losing the collateral to an early call assignment.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
